figures.finding: In New South Wales a child performer or model is anyone under sixteen, the person who casts and directs the child must hold the Children's Guardian's Authority and give 7 days' notice, and film and television work is capped by age (4 hours a day under 3 years, 6 hours at 3 to 7, 8 hours at 8 to 15, within 6 a.m. to 11 p.m.); in Victoria an employer needs a licence for anyone under fifteen, with no minimum age in entertainment, and the Code caps film and television work at 4, 6 and 8 hours a day by age.

Victoria: Child Employment Act 2003 and the Mandatory Code of Practice for the Employment of Children in Entertainment (2014), clause 22, Table A. Other States and Territories aren't read.

figures.finding: In New South Wales a person under eighteen may sign a contract that is for his benefit and that he understands; in South Australia a court may approve a minor's contract, which then binds him; neither state's pages set aside any share of a child's earnings, and neither rule is limited to performing work.

AU.02.binding: a contract for the minor's benefit that the minor understands (Minors (Property and Contracts) Act 1970 ss 18-19)

AU.05.binding: a court's consent (Minors Contracts (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 1979 s 6), or affirmation after 18

value.reachesWritingDirecting: the rules are general contract law, so they reach any work

figures.applies: New South Wales (AU.02) and South Australia (AU.05); other states not traced.

sources.said: Sign a contract to buy a mobile phone, car, motorbike, gym membership or rent a place to live 18 Or Any age as long as it is for your benefit and you understand what you are signing ss18 and 19, Minors (Property and Contracts) Act 1970

A minor may make a binding contract with the consent of a court . The minor's parents can apply on the minor’s behalf, if the minor wishes to be bound; or the other party can apply, if they wants to make the contract enforceable against the minor. If the court decides to approve the contract, it will then be legally binding [ Minors Contracts (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 1979 (SA) s 6].

figures.finding: Australia has no national minimum working age: Victoria and Queensland set 13 (11 for delivery work), Western Australia bars most work under 15 but allows shops and restaurants at 13 and deliveries at 10, the ACT bars employment under 15 save light work, New South Wales and South Australia set no age beyond keeping a child at school, and acting or performing is open at any age in Victoria and Western Australia.

AU.01.except: light work (10 hours a week, more with 7 days' written notice), family business

AU.02.note: any age, if the job doesn't stop schooling

AU.05.note: any age outside school hours; full-time from 17

figures.applies: By state and territory; Tasmania and the Northern Territory remain blocked.

sources.said: In Victoria, a child must be: 11 to deliver newspapers and advertising material 13 to deliver pharmaceutical products or do other types of work, such as retail or hospitality. There is no age limit for working in entertainment, but there are industry-specific requirements .

The Child Employment Act 2006 prohibits the employment of children below the ages specified in the Child Employment Regulation 2016 . Generally the minimum age for employment is 13. This is lowered to 11 where the child carries out supervised delivery work

As long as the work does not prevent school attendance, children of any age can: work in a family business; perform professionally as an actor, musician, entertainer or in an advertisement; … Children aged 13 and 14 Are allowed to: deliver newspapers, pamphlets or advertising material; work in a shop, fast food outlet, cafe, restaurant;

(1) A person commits an offence if— (a) the person employs a child or young person; and (b) the child or young person is under 15 years old. … (1) Section 795 (1) does not apply to the employment of a child or young person if— (a) the employment is in light work; and (b) the child or young person is employed for 10 hours per week or less.
Get a job Any age (as long as your job doesn’t stop you going to school if you haven’t completed Year 10)

You can work before reaching this age provided you do not work during school hours and the work does not interfere with your ability to attend school [Education and Children's Services Act 2019 (SA) s 74(1)].
